title: Nigeria Lion:
title_q: “Sir, Can I Ask You a Question?”
title_short: Nigeria Lion · Sir, Can I Ask You
headline: Atdhe runs after a stranger in the hall, and the stranger tells him the proudest thing he did as a Lion.
story: Atdhe chases a Lion in a red cap across the convention hall: “Sir, sir, can I ask you a question?” The man stops and answers. He likes helping people. His favourite memory is going to a hospital in Nigeria to help build an oncology centre, so people with cancer can be treated there.

Honest flag: this interview has no friendship or family line. The Hong Kong batch leads with friendship, so this cut is built on the warm stranger moment and his own personal memory, never on institutional service talk. Atdhe decides if it ships (see decisions). Keep it short and warm.
do: Open on the chase. Frame 1 is the hall, his back walking away, Atdhe's voice “Sir, sir”.
Hold his face when he turns. That turn is the friendship moment.
Keep his “sir” in the captions. It is his voice.
Let “God bless you” play. It is the warm close.
Keep the whole cut under 30 s.
dont: Don't use “You know what is charity? Do you know what is charity? You don't know.” (00:26–00:34). It reads as a lecture.
Don't add hospital or cancer B-roll. We have none, and it would make it a service ad.
No name super. The transcript name “Atbe” is not verified.
